review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Smithsonian and FishBase sources support resident rocky-shore habitat and depth occurrence; broad temperature envelope is not a preferred SST curve.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 10 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for opaleye.
factors.value_notes: FishBase reports a very broad environmental temperature envelope (0-33 °C) and a subtropical/north-temperate distribution, but this is not a preferred SST interval or a validated catch-response curve. The configured 14-22 °C range and 16-20 °C ideal remain provisional; no numeric preference should be inferred from the climate label or tolerance envelope.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for opaleye.
factors.value_notes: The Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute reports demersal rocky-shore habitat from 1-32 m; FishBase reports 2-30 m, commonly 2-6 m, and resident intertidal/kelp-bed behavior. This supports shallow coastal depth use and the 1-25 m outer band, but the 3-20 m ideal is not a measured preference curve.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.

timing.note: West Coast captain reports and biological upwelling patterns.
